title: Answer: the higher-order thought is roughly contemporaneous, and onsets are judged

statements.text: The theory gives no account of time. It requires the higher-order thought to be roughly contemporaneous with its target as a typical condition, and the empirical program holds that when something seems to begin is set by higher-order judgment, so awareness can lag the processes it is about.

sources.quote: a mental state's being conscious is its being accompanied by a roughly simultaneous higher-order thought about that very mental state
Thus, the phenomenon is likely to depend on higher-order mechanisms
